currentContext.strengths: Cost-competitive manufacturing base in India, supported by vertical integration across electrical production|Strong R&D capabilities, with DSIR-accredited facilities driving innovation and product development|Established global presence across Europe and Asia, enhancing market access and customer diversification|Advanced IoT-enabled testing infrastructure improving product quality, efficiency and reliability|Robust capabilities in EV components, including traction motors and battery management systems, aligned with global electrification trends|Strategic partnerships with leading OEMs and Tier-1 suppliers, strengthening positioning in high-growth segments such as two-wheelers and sustainable mobility|Integrated capabilities across product design, engineering, manufacturing and validation|Track record of innovation supported by a growing patent portfolio|Extensive aftermarket distribution: over 800 channel partners in India and 30+ countries globally, 8,000+ SKUs under 40+ product lines
currentContext.strategies: Build a globally competitive, technology-led automotive solutions company combining engineering depth, embedded electronics, software-enabled functionality, sustainable manufacturing, customer intimacy and disciplined execution|Prioritise profitable growth, customer diversification, product mix improvement and disciplined capital allocation across businesses|Anchor growth, profit and cash flow generation on the India business, executing across two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles and commercial vehicles|Revive and de-risk overseas operations — build a leaner, more resilient international business and take overseas electronics to an EBITDA-neutral position|Technology-led growth pillars: Electrification (EV components, emission-control aligned products, EFI and ISG); Intelligent Mobility (ADAS, driver monitoring systems, video telematics, connected clusters); Advanced Lighting & Electronics (advanced lighting technology, electronics development and localised manufacturing)|Continue investing in ADAS, driver monitoring systems and video telematics, and build capabilities ahead of industry transitions via a dedicated R&D team in China for advanced lighting technology and electronics development|Deepen localisation and vertical integration while strengthening global presence|Strengthen the aftermarket business by widening the distribution network as well as the product portfolio|Explore non-auto adjacencies, inorganic opportunities close to core areas of competency, and strategic partnerships|Deepen relationships with existing customers and expand share with global OEMs|Make the cost structure more robust — the FY26 voluntary separation scheme was aimed at improving long-term productivity and cost competitiveness|Embed sustainability as a core element of long-term growth strategy: energy efficiency, higher renewable energy use, resource conservation and waste minimisation across facilities|'Brilliance @ Scale' — embed innovation, execution discipline, customer centricity, quality, cost leadership and sustainability across every plant, function and geography|The Board has a Dividend Distribution Policy aligned with SEBI Listing Regulations, under which it recommended a final dividend of Rs 1.50 per equity share (@150% on a face value of Re.1 each) for FY 2025-26, to be declared at the 38th AGM. Credit quality is managed with India Ratings and Research: the long-term loans rating was upgraded to IND AA+/Stable during the year and short-term bank facilities and the commercial paper programme were affirmed at IND A1+, which management cites as evidence of good financial health and ability to meet obligations. The AGM notice also carries special business seeking approval for an increase in the overall borrowing limit. On governance of financial reporting, the statutory auditors issued modified opinions on both the standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY26; the Company has filed a Statement on Impact of Audit Qualifications with the stock exchanges and management states it is strengthening internal controls with a view to moving towards unmodified audit opinions in future periods. Internal auditors report directly to the Audit Committee, the Board accepted all Committee recommendations during the year, and no non-compliance of Corporate Governance Report requirements was reported.|Implementing strategic initiatives focused on energy conservation and the transition to renewable energy across all plants, wherever feasible (stated mitigation for the Energy and GHG Emissions material risk)|Implementation of a robust occupational health and safety management system including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001|Labour management and human rights: fair wages, working hours and employee engagement, with Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) and anti-discrimination measures to foster a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace|Sustainable sourcing practices and a sustainable supply chain, ensuring partnerships with suppliers committed to upholding environmental and social responsibility standards|Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI) as a driver of innovation, employee engagement and retention|Evaluation of processes and assessment to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations (regulatory compliance)|Business ethics and transparency embedded to promote ethical decision-making at all organisational levels|CSR is applicable to the Company under Section 135 of the Companies Act, 2013, with a Corporate Social Responsibility Committee acting as the grievance-redressal mechanism for communities|Stakeholder-wise grievance redressal mechanisms are in place — CSR Committee for communities, the Stakeholder Relationship Committee and compliance officer channel for shareholders and investors, and a Whistle Blower Policy for employees, workers, customers and value-chain partners; all employee/worker complaints filed during the year were resolved|BRSR FY2025-26 reported on a standalone basis with no external assurance provider appointed (type of assurance: Not Applicable)
currentContext.expansion: Varroc's expansion is expressed as footprint and capability build-out rather than as a named project pipeline. The Company operates multiple manufacturing facilities and R&D centres across India, Europe and Asia. Under Business II, electronics manufacturing sits in Romania, India and Vietnam, supported by R&D centres in Poland, Germany, China and India, while global lighting manufacturing is supported by facilities in India, Thailand, Italy, Romania and Vietnam with engineering centres across Europe and Asia; R&D centres are cited in India, Poland, Italy, China and Vietnam. During FY26 the Company set up a dedicated R&D team in China for advanced lighting technology and to support electronics development, describing it as building capabilities ahead of industry transitions. Localised production of two-wheeler and three-wheeler EV components in India began in 2022, and the product portfolio has since been expanded into fuel-efficient products such as EFI and ISG. Overseas, business wins from highly advanced technology OEMs for the Romania and Thailand operations are expected to help establish the lighting and electronics business globally, with overseas electronics targeted to reach an EBITDA-neutral position by the end of FY27. Business I manufacturing remains largely concentrated in India, supported by an extensive distribution and service network — the aftermarket division runs over 800 channel partners in India and 30+ countries globally, with 8,000+ SKUs under 40+ product lines served from a 1,60,000 sq. ft warehouse. Capacity actions during the year were also cost-structure led: a Voluntary Separation Scheme for permanent workmen across various Group manufacturing facilities drew 432 applications of which 411 were accepted, and the scheme concluded on January 16, 2026. No specific rupee capex programme, plant commissioning date or capacity addition figure is disclosed in this section of the report.

risks.risk: Energy consumption and GHG emissions from manufacturing
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table as a Risk with negative financial implications — GHG emissions from manufacturing significantly contribute to climate change, and these processes typically demand considerable energy for machinery, heating, cooling and lighting; mitigation is strategic energy conservation and transition to renewable energy across all plants wherever feasible.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as both Risk and Opportunity — non-compliance may result in fines, legal penalties and litigation, adversely affecting both financial performance and brand reputation; mitigated through evaluation of processes and assessment to ensure compliance with applicable laws and regulations.

Flagged in the BRSR material-issues table as both Risk and Opportunity — ethical business practices and transparency foster stakeholder trust and promote ethical decision-making at all organisational levels.

100% of the entity's turnover comes from the manufacture and sale of automotive components, tying the business entirely to the automotive cycle; within that, Electrical & Lighting auto parts (41.41%) and Polymer auto parts (34.83%) account for the bulk of turnover, so product-line concentration compounds the sector concentration.

risks.risk: Limited export diversification at the listed-entity level
risks.note: Exports contribute only 3.8% of the entity's total turnover on the standalone reporting boundary, leaving the listed entity heavily dependent on domestic demand even though it serves both domestic and international OEMs and an aftermarket presence in over 27 countries.

Turnover rate for permanent employees rose to 17.46% in FY 2026 from 16.60% in FY 2025 and 15% in FY 2024, with female permanent-employee attrition higher at 22.57% — a structural talent-retention risk as mobility technology capabilities become scarcer.

risks.risk: Workforce restructuring and labour relations across manufacturing facilities
risks.note: The Group implemented a Voluntary Separation Scheme for permanent workmen across various manufacturing facilities to streamline the workforce and optimise operating costs; 432 applications were received, 411 accepted, and the scheme concluded on January 16, 2026 — execution of such cost actions carries near-term profitability and industrial-relations implications.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety in manufacturing operations
risks.note: Identified in the BRSR material-issues table (as an opportunity with positive implications) — a secure work environment minimises accidents and occupational hazards while enhancing morale and productivity; addressed through a robust occupational health and safety management system including ISO 14001 and ISO 45001.

risks.risk: Board and senior-management gender diversity gap
risks.note: BRSR representation disclosure shows 0% female representation on the Board of Directors and 0% among Key Management Personnel, with women forming 25% of Independent Directors only — a governance/social exposure given the Company's own stated focus on Diversity, Equity & Inclusion.

Identified as a material issue — a sustainable supply chain improves operational efficiency, transparency and environmental impact across the value chain, and requires suppliers committed to environmental and social responsibility standards.

themes.title: Auto components & EV-driveline localization
themes.need: Premiumization, content-per-vehicle rise and EV/hybrid transition pull a deep auto-ancillary chain - MOTHERSON/SONACOMS/BOSCHLTD/SCHAEFFLER/SKFINDIA/UNOMINDA-tier on driveline, bearings, wiring (MSUMI) and EV systems; OLAELEC/ATHERENERG/OLECTRA on EV OEMs (OLAELEC targeting cell-to-pack 10-15% cost edge); SUNDRMFAST/ENDURANCE/CRAFTSMAN/BHARATFORG on forgings/machining. Q1FY27 showed contracted pricing finally landing for Tier-2s: SSWL earned EBITDA/wheel of Rs 314 against Rs 262 YoY, which management attributed mostly to two years of OEM input-price increases finally landing (1-5%, more pending) rather than mix, with all plants above 95% utilisation and knuckles at 100%; KROSS delivered a 12.23% EBITDA margin (+63bps) BEFORE two retrospective pass-throughs land (steel settled ~15 July, the CV conversion-cost settlement still pending), making Q1 a floor rather than a peak.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull; retrospective OEM price pass-throughs still to land (KROSS CV conversion cost); EV cell/Gigafactory ramps (OLAELEC 6GWh by June); export + new-platform content wins.

products.body:

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India remained the fastest-growing major economy, with resilient domestic demand, moderating inflation, easing interest rates and continued investment in manufacturing, infrastructure and mobility
- GST rate rationalisation on automobiles in the second half unlocked demand across every segment the Company serves, and rural and urban consumption converged for the first time in three years
- Growing contribution from electric vehicles — EV revenue contributed around 13% for the full year, and order wins were strongly skewed towards EV and future-facing platforms
- Order wins from highly advanced technology OEMs for the Romania and Thailand operations are expected to help establish the lighting and electronics business globally
- Recovery in growth has already started in overseas operations after a period of market weakness, customer concentration and cost pressure
- Business alignment with industry megatrends — electrification, safety, smart mobility, lightweighting, premiumisation and localisation
- Structural Indian demand drivers — rising income levels, infrastructure development, premiumisation, regulatory evolution and electrification
- Globally, the move towards resilient supply chains, regionalisation and technology-led sourcing can create new opportunities for companies with strong execution and engineering depth
- Headwinds navigated during the year: a rare-earth magnet supply squeeze, a stubbornly weak European automotive market, and an increasingly complicated global tariff environment
- Rising tariff barriers, geopolitical tensions, supply-chain restrictions and increasing regionalisation reinforce the importance of resilience, localisation, technology depth and capital discipline
- For the full year, net new business wins were approximately H32,890 million in annualised peak revenue, with around 65% related to EV models
- Business wins from highly advanced technology OEMs for Romania and Thailand operations will help establish the lighting and electronics business globally
- Management describes a robust business pipeline and expanding customer base underpinning confidence in the next phase of growth

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Varroc's expansion is expressed as footprint and capability build-out rather than as a named project pipeline. The Company operates multiple manufacturing facilities and R&D centres across India, Europe and Asia. Under Business II, electronics manufacturing sits in Romania, India and Vietnam, supported by R&D centres in Poland, Germany, China and India, while global lighting manufacturing is supported by facilities in India, Thailand, Italy, Romania and Vietnam with engineering centres across Europe and Asia; R&D centres are cited in India, Poland, Italy, China and Vietnam. During FY26 the Company set up a dedicated R&D team in China for advanced lighting technology and to support electronics development, describing it as building capabilities ahead of industry transitions. Localised production of two-wheeler and three-wheeler EV components in India began in 2022, and the product portfolio has since been expanded into fuel-efficient products such as EFI and ISG. Overseas, business wins from highly advanced technology OEMs for the Romania and Thailand operations are expected to help establish the lighting and electronics business globally, with overseas electronics targeted to reach an EBITDA-neutral position by the end of FY27. Business I manufacturing remains largely concentrated in India, supported by an extensive distribution and service network — the aftermarket division runs over 800 channel partners in India and 30+ countries globally, with 8,000+ SKUs under 40+ product lines served from a 1,60,000 sq. ft warehouse. Capacity actions during the year were also cost-structure led: a Voluntary Separation Scheme for permanent workmen across various Group manufacturing facilities drew 432 applications of which 411 were accepted, and the scheme concluded on January 16, 2026. No specific rupee capex programme, plant commissioning date or capacity addition figure is disclosed in this section of the report.

other.title: Notable from the deck
